cases.problem: Issue #2449: request throughput regressed significantly in axum 0.7 for routers with many routes, partly because the `Router` (and its route table) is cloned per connection/request. Make cloning a `Router` cheap.

rejected.title: Internally `Arc` `Router`
rejected.approach: Stores router state as `inner: Arc<RouterInner<S>>` and uses `Arc::try_unwrap`/clone-on-write in builder methods. It is stacked on #2473, which adds `Sync` bounds to handlers, layers and internal erased types (`ErasedIntoRoute<S, E>: Send + Sync`, `H: Clone + Send + Sync`, `LayerFn: ... + Send + Sync`) so that the router can be shared — a breaking API change.

reason.quote: https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum/pull/2476 is currently based on https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum/pull/2473, which is a breaking change. Thus, we can't ship it in a patch release for 0.7 to recover performance of existing apps that have upgraded to axum 0.7.
Not sure if we still require `Sync` for services or if the mutex approach is fine.

accepted.title: Internally `Arc` `Router`, without breaking changes
accepted.approach: Applies the same `Arc<RouterInner<S>>` change on top of #2481, which wraps the non-`Sync` boxed pieces in a mutex (`BoxedIntoRoute<S, E>(AxumMutex<Box<dyn ErasedIntoRoute<S, E>>>)`, `AxumMutex` in axum/src/util.rs that counts locks in tests) so `Router` becomes `Sync` without new trait bounds; adds a test asserting the lock is not taken per request.

distinguishing_signals: rejected: adds `+ Sync` to public/internal bounds (handlers, layers, `ErasedIntoRoute`) — breaking
accepted: no new `Sync` bounds; introduces `AxumMutex` / `Mutex` wrapper around boxed erased routes
both: `inner: Arc<RouterInner<S>>` in axum/src/routing/mod.rs

reason.quote: I've realized that this API can still be misused as you can do this: ... I'll convert this to a draft while I explore other paths.

reason.quote: I think this would be brittle for what you're trying to achieve. You would have to call the method on every single method router in your app. ... Finally, I think what you're really looking for is `method_not_allowed_fallback`.

accepted.approach: Implements `JoinMap<K, V, S>` in tokio-util (tokio-util/src/task/join_map.rs, `tokio_util::task::JoinMap`) on top of public tokio APIs: a `JoinSet` plus a `HashMap` of `AbortHandle`s keyed via the new task IDs (#4630), with `spawn`, `spawn_on`, `spawn_local`, `join_one -> Option<(K, Result<V, JoinError>)>`, `abort(key)`. Requires `tokio_unstable` cfg (.cargo/config).

distinguishing_signals: rejected: new file tokio/src/task/join_map.rs (inside the tokio crate)
rejected: modifies tokio/src/util/idle_notified_set.rs
accepted: new file tokio-util/src/task/join_map.rs; tokio-util/Cargo.toml bumps tokio dependency
accepted: keys tracked through task Id / AbortHandle rather than in tokio internals
cases.notes: Same author (hawkw) for both; a prerequisite PR (#4630 task IDs) was merged between them. The rejection is about crate placement / API commitment.

cases.problem: Deeply nested `FuturesUnordered` workloads where most leaf futures are ready suffer from Tokio's cooperative scheduling budget: forced yields cause huge numbers of useless polls (observed ~50% CPU in `wake_by_ref` from `poll_proceed`). Users need a way to opt out of cooperative scheduling.

rejected.title: coop: allow disabling cooperative scheduling
rejected.approach: Adds a runtime-wide switch `runtime::Builder::no_coop(&mut self)` (tokio/src/runtime/builder.rs) that is threaded through the schedulers (basic_scheduler, thread_pool worker, LocalSet, enter) so `coop` budgeting is disabled for every task on that runtime. Targeted the 0.2.x branch.

reason.quote: I'm worried about the next user of tokio that comes along, finds some problem that they think is due to coop, throw in a `no_coop()` call on their runtime constructor, and then forgets about it. And then complains about weird tail latency spikes in tokio :)
I guess now that #3547 is merged, we should just close this?

accepted.title: coop: expose an unconstrained() opt-out
accepted.approach: Adds a per-future opt-out: `tokio::task::unconstrained(fut) -> Unconstrained<F>` (tokio/src/task/unconstrained.rs) whose `poll` runs the inner future inside `coop::with_unconstrained`, a new pub(crate) helper in tokio/src/coop.rs. No runtime Builder change.

distinguishing_signals: rejected: new `Builder::no_coop()` method; runtime-wide flag plumbed into schedulers
accepted: new file tokio/src/task/unconstrained.rs with `pub fn unconstrained` and `pub struct Unconstrained<F>`
accepted: no changes to tokio/src/runtime/builder.rs
cases.notes: Same author (krallin); the accepted PR was opened during the review discussion (parallel). Rejected PR targeted v0.2.x, accepted targeted 1.x master, so file layouts differ. Key rejection voice (jonhoo) was a Tokio contributor/reviewer.
cases.problem_original: Deeply nested `FuturesUnordered` workloads where most leaf futures are ready suffer from Tokio's cooperative scheduling budget: forced yields cause huge numbers of useless polls (observed ~50% CPU in `wake_by_ref` from `poll_proceed`). Users need a way to opt out of cooperative scheduling for code that does not work well with it.
cases.problem_edit: 'For code' points at the per-future opt-out that was accepted.
cases.role_reason: The rejected attempt and its reason are visible at the accepted base commit.

cases.problem: Users frequently want a spawned task to be cancelled automatically when the handle to it is dropped (structured-concurrency style), but `JoinHandle` detaches the task on drop. Provide a utility in tokio-util for tying a spawned task's lifetime to a handle.

rejected.title: feat: added spawn_aborting
rejected.approach: Adds a public module tokio-util/src/task/spawn_aborting.rs with a free function `spawn_aborting<F>(future) -> DropHandle<F::Output>` that calls `tokio::spawn` and a `pub struct DropHandle<T>(JoinHandle<T>)` whose `Drop` aborts; exposes inner handle access instead of wrapper methods.

reason.quote: I don't like this name. It sounds like something that would immediately make something abort.

My personal preference would be to make the spawn function a function on the `DropHandle` type. IMO, we also ought to have a `DropHandle::new()` constructor that takes a `JoinHandle`, so that the abort-on-drop behavior can be added to `JoinHandle`s returned by `tokio::task::spawn_local` or `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`.

accepted.title: Add `AbortOnDropHandle` type
accepted.approach: Adds `tokio_util::task::AbortOnDropHandle<T>(JoinHandle<T>)` (tokio-util/src/task/abort_on_drop.rs) constructed from any existing JoinHandle via `AbortOnDropHandle::new(handle)`, with wrapper methods `abort`, `is_finished`, `abort_handle`, a `Future` impl, and abort in `Drop`. No spawn function.

distinguishing_signals: rejected: free fn `pub fn spawn_aborting` that spawns internally; type named `DropHandle`
accepted: `pub struct AbortOnDropHandle<T>` with `pub fn new(handle: JoinHandle<T>)`
accepted: new file tokio-util/src/task/abort_on_drop.rs and tests/abort_on_drop.rs
cases.notes: Rejected PR stalled after review; it was closed by Darksonn as 'added in #6786'. The objections are API-shape/naming, recorded months before #6786.
cases.role_reason: The rejected attempt and its reason are visible at the accepted base commit.

cases.problem: Issue #3903: users want a collection that owns a set of spawned tasks, lets them await whichever task finishes next, and aborts the remaining tasks when the collection is dropped. Provide such a task-set type.

rejected.title: add taskset api
rejected.approach: Adds `TaskSet<T>` in tokio-util/src/taskset.rs built purely on public `JoinHandle`s stored in a collection, with `next_finished` polling every handle (O(n)), plus a `TaskSetStream` wrapper in tokio-stream (tokio-stream/src/wrappers/task.rs).

reason.quote: You're probably going to need some sort of custom waker to get around it.
putting it in Tokio itself is an option since you can then put the data in the task object itself.

accepted.title: Add `JoinSet`
accepted.approach: Adds `tokio::task::JoinSet<T>` (tokio/src/task/join_set.rs) inside the tokio crate using a new `IdleNotifiedSet` (tokio/src/util/idle_notified_set.rs) on top of the intrusive `linked_list`, plus a task-internal join waker hook (`set_join_waker` in runtime/task/join.rs, harness.rs, raw.rs) so completion is O(1); includes loom tests.

distinguishing_signals: rejected: new tokio-util/src/taskset.rs and tokio-stream wrapper; iterates all JoinHandles to find a finished one
accepted: new tokio/src/task/join_set.rs and tokio/src/util/idle_notified_set.rs
accepted: modifies tokio/src/runtime/task/{join,harness,raw}.rs (join waker plumbing)
cases.notes: Inverse of tokio-4538: here the accepted design moved INTO tokio core because efficient implementation needs task internals. Accepted PR (by maintainer) was opened while the rejected one was still open; review comments predate it.
cases.problem_original: Issue #3903: users want a collection that owns a set of spawned tasks, lets them await whichever task finishes next, and aborts the remaining tasks when the collection is dropped. Provide such a task-set type with efficient (not O(n) per completion) waiting.
cases.problem_edit: The parenthetical is the reviewers' objection to the rejected design.
cases.role_reason: The rejected attempt and its reason are visible at the accepted base commit.

cases.problem: In Tokio 1.0 the `mpsc::Sender` lost its poll-based `poll_ready`/`try_send` style API, so code that implements `Sink` or other poll-based interfaces on top of a bounded mpsc sender has no good way to do so. Provide a poll-based wrapper around `tokio::sync::mpsc::Sender` in tokio-util that does not allocate per sent item.

rejected.title: Add tokio02-style mpsc sender
rejected.approach: Adds a generic `pollify` module (tokio-util/src/pollify.rs: `trait AsyncOp`, `struct Pollify<A>`) and a lifetime-parameterised `Sender<'a, T>` in tokio-util/src/sync/mpsc.rs that stores the in-flight `reserve()` future in a self-referential pinned struct using `unsafe` (`FutureBox` with `unsafe impl Send/Sync`, `map_unchecked_mut`).

reason.quote: It involves some serious unsafe code to soundly build a self-referential struct, and there are some things I would have to try out in miri before I am happy with it.

Closing this, as I have just opened #3490, which implements this without unsafe, while still avoiding allocating for every sent item. The new PR also avoids the lifetime issues that this PR runs into.

accepted.title: Add pollable mpsc::Sender
accepted.approach: Adds `tokio_util::sync::PollSender<T>` (tokio-util/src/sync/mpsc.rs) holding the reserve future in the safe `ReusableBoxFuture` utility (no per-send allocation), with `start_send`, `poll_send_done`, `is_ready`, `is_closed`, `clone_inner`; no lifetime parameter.

distinguishing_signals: rejected: new generic tokio-util/src/pollify.rs module and `unsafe impl` blocks
rejected: `pub struct Sender<'a, T>` with a lifetime parameter
accepted: `pub struct PollSender<T>` using `ReusableBoxFuture`, no new unsafe
accepted: only touches tokio-util/src/sync/{mod,mpsc}.rs and tokio-util/tests/mpsc.rs
cases.notes: Accepted PR opened by the reviewer minutes before closing the rejected one; the 'serious unsafe' concern predates it by six weeks.
cases.role_reason: The rejected attempt and its reason are visible at the accepted base commit.

cases.problem: Issue #3350: `mpsc::Receiver::try_recv` was removed before Tokio 1.0 because it could return `Empty` while a send had already completed (a racing sender reserved an earlier slot but had not finished writing). Bring back `try_recv` for bounded and unbounded mpsc receivers with correct semantics: it must not report `Empty` when a message whose send has completed is in the channel.

rejected.title: sync: Add `try_recv` back
rejected.approach: Distinguishes 'slot not ready' from 'empty' inside the block list: adds `Read::NotReady`, a `HAS_NEXT` bit in each block's `ready_slots`, and `write_in_progress()` look-ahead logic in tokio/src/sync/mpsc/block.rs, then has `try_recv` in chan.rs loop/spin (later: park on an extra `not_ready_waker: AtomicWaker`) until the in-progress write lands.

reason.quote: Generally speaking, we try to avoid spinning. It’s going to be tricky to avoid that here though.
We did not end up accepting it because it was complicated and a simpler solution was available, but the solution that just got merged used several ideas from your PR

accepted.title: sync: implement try_recv for mpsc channels
accepted.approach: Adds `list::Rx::try_pop` returning a new `TryPopResult { Ok, Empty, Closed, Busy }` (tokio/src/sync/mpsc/list.rs); `chan::Rx::try_recv` returns on Ok/Empty/Closed and on `Busy` wakes any registered `rx_waker`, registers a `CachedParkThread` waker in the existing `rx_waker` slot and parks the thread until the racing send completes. Adds `TryRecvError` and `try_recv` on bounded/unbounded receivers.

distinguishing_signals: rejected: modifies tokio/src/sync/mpsc/block.rs (new `HAS_NEXT` bit, `Read::NotReady`, `write_in_progress`)
rejected: new field `not_ready_waker: AtomicWaker` in chan
accepted: `enum TryPopResult` with `Busy` variant in list.rs; block.rs untouched
accepted: `CachedParkThread` + existing `rx_waker.register_by_ref`
cases.notes: Rejected PR is not a pure spin in its final revision (it also parks), so the diff-level difference is mostly block.rs bit-tricks vs a list-level Busy result. Accepted PR opened by the reviewer while rejected PR was open.
cases.role_reason: The rejected attempt and its reason are visible at the accepted base commit.

cases.problem: Issue #3373: `tokio::fs` lacks an async equivalent of checking whether a path exists (std offers `Path::exists`), so users write `fs::metadata(path).await.is_ok()`. Add an async function to `tokio::fs` for checking whether a path exists.

rejected.title: Add `fs::exists` function
rejected.approach: Adds `pub async fn exists(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> bool` in tokio/src/fs/exists.rs mirroring `std::path::Path::exists` (metadata via spawn_blocking, mapping any error to `false`), re-exported from tokio::fs.

reason.quote: Returning `io::Result<bool>` is much better than `metadata_accessible`. That's an awful name.
I mean, are you should people will do `unwrap_or(false)` if we make it return a `Result`? They'll probably question mark it instead, propagating it on a permissions error.

accepted.title: Add `fs::try_exists`
accepted.approach: Adds `pub async fn try_exists(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> io::Result<bool>` in tokio/src/fs/try_exists.rs (mirroring the then-unstable `std::fs::try_exists`), returning `Ok(false)` only for NotFound and propagating other errors; adds tokio/tests/fs_try_exists.rs.

distinguishing_signals: rejected: `fn exists(...) -> bool` in tokio/src/fs/exists.rs
accepted: `fn try_exists(...) -> io::Result<bool>` in tokio/src/fs/try_exists.rs
accepted: test that a permission-denied path yields Err, not false
cases.notes: Rejected PR stalled and was closed after the accepted one merged (closure reason: 'since #4299 was merged'), but the design objection (bool vs io::Result<bool>) was recorded in Jan 2021, before #4299 was opened. Problem statement's last clause hints at the answer; drop 'handling errors such as permission denied correctly' for a harder variant. Part of the critique came from a non-member (Kixunil).
cases.problem_original: Issue #3373: `tokio::fs` lacks an async equivalent of checking whether a path exists (std offers `Path::exists`), so users write `fs::metadata(path).await.is_ok()`. Add an async function to `tokio::fs` for checking whether a path exists, handling errors such as permission denied correctly.
cases.problem_edit: The clause about permission-denied errors is the maintainers' objection to the rejected design.
cases.role_reason: The rejected attempt and its reason are visible at the accepted base commit.

cases.problem: Issues #2965/#3096: code that only has a `tokio::runtime::Handle` (not the owning `Runtime`) cannot block on a future, e.g. when implementing a synchronous trait from inside a thread that has a handle. Add the ability to block on a future through a runtime `Handle`.

rejected.title: rt: move block_on to handle
rejected.approach: Moves the `block_on` machinery from `Runtime` to `Handle` (tokio/src/runtime/handle.rs: `Handle::block_on`, `block_on_with_basic_scheduler`), making the handle able to take the basic scheduler's core via new `take_inner()`/`InnerGuard` and `notify()` in tokio/src/runtime/basic_scheduler.rs; `Runtime::block_on` delegates to it. No special handling for runtime shutdown.

reason.quote: How does this handle the case where you shut down the runtime while a handle is blocking on something?
A handle should not hold ownership of any of the scheduler components (like the task queue).
It will just hang and this is bad UX/hard to debug.

accepted.title: rt: add Handle::block_on
accepted.approach: Adds `Handle::block_on` that drives the future on the current thread without taking scheduler ownership, and makes runtime resources fail once the runtime is shut down: timer driver gets an `Inner`/`InnerState` with shutdown flag (tokio/src/time/driver/{mod,handle,entry}.rs), I/O `registration.rs` and blocking fs ops return errors, new `util/error.rs` messages; tests in tokio/tests/rt_handle_block_on.rs.

distinguishing_signals: rejected: new pub(crate) `take_inner()` / `InnerGuard` on basic_scheduler so a Handle can own the core
accepted: no basic_scheduler changes; changes time driver and io registration to error after shutdown
accepted: new test file tokio/tests/rt_handle_block_on.rs
cases.notes: Accepted PR continues maintainer draft #3549 and was opened (by an Embark contributor, merged by davidpdrsn) after the shutdown objection; the rejected PR was closed only later. Big multi-file change; harder eval case.
cases.problem_original: Issues #2965/#3096: code that only has a `tokio::runtime::Handle` (not the owning `Runtime`) cannot block on a future, e.g. when implementing a synchronous trait from inside a thread that has a handle. Add the ability to block on a future through a runtime `Handle`, with well-defined behaviour when the runtime is shut down while something is blocked through a handle.
cases.problem_edit: The clause is the maintainers' objection to the rejected design.
cases.role_reason: The rejected attempt and its reason are visible at the accepted base commit.

method: Searched tokio-rs/axum closed-unmerged PRs (search_pull_requests 'repo:tokio-rs/axum is:pr is:closed is:unmerged comments:>3', sorted by comments, ~130 hits) plus phrase searches on closed-unmerged PRs ('superseded by', 'in favor of', 'instead', 'rather than', 'better fix', 'went ahead', 'axum-extra') and merged PRs ('supersedes', 'alternative to', 'in favor of'). Read issue/review comments only for promising candidates, then located the merged alternative via linked PR numbers or targeted searches. axum yielded 13 accepted cases (<15), so sampled BurntSushi/ripgrep (low yield, see rejected_candidates) and then tokio-rs/tokio ('is:closed is:unmerged comments:>4', ~300 hits, top ~100 triaged). Files and base SHAs were computed from partial clones (git fetch refs/pull/N/head; files = git diff --name-only merge-base..head; base_sha = merge-base with the default branch, which matched the API base for every accepted PR checked); overrides noted per case (axum#1848 uses its v0.7.0 branch base; axum#1766 diffed from the v0.7.0 branch tip it was based on; tokio#3516 targeted v0.2.x). Quotes are verbatim maintainer/reviewer text with comment URLs.
curation: Problem statements that restated the maintainers' objection or pointed at the accepted mechanism were edited; the original text is kept in problem_original with the reason in problem_edit. Cases where the objection was posted only after the accepted work began are role=control: history could not have helped there.
